title: The useContext Hook
description: Master consuming context values with the useContext hook.

data.text: **useContext** is the hook for consuming context values. It accepts a context object and returns the current context value from the nearest Provider above the calling component.
Call `useContext` at the top level of your component. It returns whatever value the nearest Provider supplied.

data.title: useContext

data.text: Context values are often objects that include both data and updater functions. Destructure them for readability.

items.question: What if I forget to wrap a component in a Provider?
items.answer: useContext returns the default value passed to createContext. Use a custom hook with an error check to catch this early.

items.question: Does useContext cause re-renders?
items.answer: Yes. Any component that calls useContext re-renders when the Provider value changes. Split contexts to limit the blast radius.

items.question: Can I update context from a consumer?
items.answer: Yes. Include updater functions in the Provider value, or use the useState setter inside the Provider and pass it down.

items.question: Should I memoize the Provider value?
items.answer: If the value is an object or array created inline, wrap it in useMemo to avoid unnecessary re-renders of consumers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useContext reads the nearest Provider value.
Wrap context consumption in a custom hook for error safety.
Multiple contexts can be consumed in the same component.
Memoize Provider values to avoid extra re-renders.
data.takeaway: useContext is the cleanest way to consume global data. Next, you will learn useRef for DOM access and mutable values.
